subject.title: Feature: Handle Signal message edits (editMessage envelope)

question: For a Signal message edit, should OpenClaw update/replace the prior session context and suppress automatic dispatch by default, or should it retain both versions with explicit edit metadata and a narrower reply policy?
rationale: The transport event can be parsed mechanically, but transcript replacement, deduplication, and interaction with an already-running agent turn are user-visible session-policy choices that should not be inferred from the closed unmerged PR.

options.title: Define edit-aware session updates
options.body: Adopt an explicit Signal edit path that relates the target timestamp to the original message, updates the session representation, and prevents an unmentioned edit from starting a second automatic reply.

options.title: Preserve both versions as metadata
options.body: Keep the original and edited content as distinct session events with structured linkage, then define a narrow dispatch rule without transcript replacement.

recommendation.title: Define edit-aware session updates
recommendation.body: Adopt an explicit Signal edit path that relates the target timestamp to the original message, updates the session representation, and prevents an unmentioned edit from starting a second automatic reply.
